subject: Reserved capacity pricing and approval roadmap for Sapphire Health
body:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity proposal for Sapphire — ask: pricing path and approval gates

Team,

Sapphire Health is asking for a 12-month reserved capacity commitment to support their new inference pipeline (clinical triage model + embeddings). High-level ask from buyer: 120 A100-equivalent GPUs, 12-month tenor, start Nov 1. They have asked for price protection clauses tied to GPU market swings and an up-front discount to get the initial commit.

I attached a proforma (proforma-pricing-sheet.xlsx) with two options:
- Option A: 12-month firm commit, SKU mix pinned, 22% list discount (higher discount to win).
- Option B: 12-month tiered commit, 18% discount upfront + capped gpu-price-pass-through (see sheet).

Primary asks for internal clarity:
- What approval path do we need if we go >18% discount?
- Can Finance sign off on a capped pass-through clause (we propose pass-through up to +/-10% of GPU input cost, capped at 5% per quarter)?
- Ops: can we guarantee allocation start date given scheduling for Nov 1?

Attachments: proforma-pricing-sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet), Sapphire_MA_plan_v1.pdf (draft mutual action plan)

Thanks — OLGA

--
Olga Petrov
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0189

On Tue, 12 Sep 2028 11:33:00 -0700, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
> To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
> Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 11:33:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal for Sapphire — ask: pricing path and approval gates
> 
> Thanks Olga — quick ops/technical notes:
> - SKU mix: 60% A100-80GB, 40% A40-equivalent for embeddings; if they require full A100s we need to adjust list price + provisioning window.
> - Lead time: provisioning confirmed for Nov 1 if contract fully executed by Oct 10. Anything after Oct 10 moves start into December.
> - Fallback plan: propose a soft fallback to dedicated shared pool with guaranteed burst windows if inventory shifts — that reduces our exposure without losing the deal.
> 
> On pass-through mechanics: ops prefers a simple formula (monthly index tied to Nvidia public spot price) with a 3% quarterly smoothing floor to avoid churn. I know legal will want simpler language.
> 
> Karthik
> Director, Dedicated Deployments
> 
On Tue, 12 Sep 2028 15:45:00 -0700, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
> To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
> Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 15:45:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal for Sapphire — ask: pricing path and approval gates
> 
> Team — ran margin sims on both options:
> - Option A (22%): gross margin erosion hits ~10 pts vs standard list; take rate sensitivity is high if GPU spot prices rebound. Requires CRO sign-off.
> - Option B (18% + capped pass-through): margins healthier (~+5 pts vs A) and exposure to GPU swings limited under the cap scenario. Finance prefers this.
> 
> Approval thresholds: discounts up to 15% — Sales lead can approve. 15–20% requires VP Sales (Marissa). >20% requires CRO + Finance exec (Ben).
> For any pass-through language, Legal needs a final read; Finance wants a clause that conservatively models a 20% GPU spike to ensure our cash flow doesn't go negative.
> 
> I can sign off on Option B if we keep the effective guarantee window (start date) pinned and the pass-through cap at 6% annually (1.5% quarterly). Anything looser needs CFO review.
> 
> Ben
> Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
> 
On Wed, 13 Sep 2028 10:02:00 -0700, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
> To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
> Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2028 10:02:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal for Sapphire — ask: pricing path and approval gates
> 
> Thanks for the modeling, Ben. My recommendation: present Option B to the customer (18% + capped pass-through) as the commercial preferred path. It's easier to get internal sign-off quickly and is defensible.
> 
> If Sapphire pushes back, we can agree to an escalation path: VP Sales approval for an additional 2% (to 20%), CRO sign-off required beyond that. I'll take ownership to get CRO aligned if we need to go there — please flag if you need me to loop him now.
> 
> Ops/Timing: Karthik, confirm the provisioning calendar in the shared doc. If we can secure Nov 1 and a contract by Oct 6, I'll go to the CRO with a clean ask.
> 
> Marissa Cole
> VP, Enterprise Sales
>

> Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0700
> Subject: Redwood reserved capacity offer — Sapphire Health (DEAL-9742)

> Hi Emma,
> 
> Great conversation yesterday — as discussed, attached is our proposed mutual action plan and a proforma that walks through two commercial options. Summary:
>
> Option B (recommended): 12-month reserved commit, 120 A100-equivalent GPUs, 18% upfront discount, capped GPU-price pass-through (max 6% annually, 1.5% quarterly smoothing).
>
> Key customer benefits: predictable unit economics for the year, priority allocation windows for Nov/Dec provisioning, standard Redwood operational SLAs.
>
> Next steps I propose:
> 1) Review the attached draft MA and proforma with procurement.
> 2) Run our SOC2 evidence packet (I copied procurement to coordinate).
> 3) If acceptable, target a signed MSA/Order by Oct 6 to secure Nov 1 start.
>
> Attachments: Sapphire_MA_plan_v1.pdf (draft), proforma-pricing-sheet.xlsx
> 
> Quick ask for procurement: any internal deadlines or approval gates we should be aware of?
>
> Thanks — looking forward to making this simple.
>
> Best,
> Olga
> Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
> olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0189
